The story is a grounded, atmospheric slice-of-life piece that avoids overused tropes, melodramatic plots, and stock expressions. Instead of relying on clichés, it builds its quiet tension through specific, realistic sensory details (the smell of low-tide mud, the hum of the ferry cable, the specific local geography of the Elbe river region) and understated character interactions. Even the conflict at the end—an unanswered phone call from someone named Jonas—is handled with restraint and ambiguity rather than predictable drama.
